steps.name: Load counts/metadata, QC filter, build DESeqDataSet
caveats: Data context reports counts.csv as 12000 x 25 (genes x samples) but metadata.csv as 24 x 4 (samples x fields) — a 25 vs 24 sample count mismatch must be explicitly checked and resolved (e.g. an extra gene-symbol or index column miscounted, or a genuinely unmatched sample) before any modeling; do not silently drop or duplicate a sample
Verify time_hours values map consistently to the four discrete time labels t0..t3 so time can be treated as a factor with 4 levels, not a continuous covariate, matching the stated 2x4 design
steps.question: Do the raw counts (12000 genes x 25 samples) and metadata (24 x 4: condition, time, time_hours) align correctly, and which genes pass a minimal expression filter for the condition x time design?
acceptance_criteria: Sample identifiers in counts.csv columns match metadata.csv rows exactly (report any mismatch, e.g. the counts matrix reporting 25 samples vs metadata's 24 rows must be reconciled and explained before proceeding)
condition and time (t0..t3) columns are parsed as factors with t0 set as the reference level
Low-count genes (e.g. sum across samples below a stated threshold, or fewer than 3 samples with count >= 10) are filtered out and the number of genes retained is reported
A DESeqDataSet is constructed with design = ~condition + time + condition:time and saved for downstream steps

steps.name: DESeq2 LRT: full (condition+time+condition:time) vs reduced (condition+time)
caveats: With only n=3 replicates per condition:time cell, power for a multi-df interaction LRT is limited — report this explicitly rather than implying the padj threshold captures all true interaction genes

The condition:time interaction in DESeq2 with a 4-level time factor is a 3-df test (three interaction coefficients); do not reduce this to a single coefficient's Wald test, which would only capture one time-contrast rather than the overall interaction
steps.question: Which genes show a significant condition:time interaction — i.e., a treatment-specific trajectory across t0..t3 beyond the trend shared by both conditions?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq() is run with test='LRT', full model ~condition + time + condition:time, reduced model ~condition + time
Output table has per-gene LRT p-value, BH-adjusted padj, and log fold-change columns for each condition:time interaction coefficient
Genes are ranked and thresholded at padj < 0.05 (report count of significant interaction genes; if zero, state that explicitly rather than lowering the threshold silently)
Full results table (all genes, not just significant ones) is saved for downstream pathway/network steps

steps.name: Characterize temporal shape of interaction genes per condition
caveats: Use variance-stabilized or rlog-transformed values for visualization, not raw counts, to avoid mean-variance artifacts dominating the heatmap
steps.question: For genes with a significant condition:time interaction, what does the per-condition trajectory across t0..t3 look like (magnitude, direction, and time point of divergence)?
acceptance_criteria: For each significant interaction gene, per-condition mean (or model-fitted) normalized expression at t0, t1, t2, t3 is computed and reported
Genes are grouped/clustered by qualitative trajectory pattern (e.g. divergence appearing early vs late, one condition flat vs the other moving) using the fitted values, not raw counts
A heatmap or line-plot visualization of scaled trajectories for the top interaction genes (by padj) is produced
Report distinguishes genes with a clear early-divergence pattern from genes with only a late-timepoint difference, since both satisfy the LRT but have different biological implications

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treatment-specific interaction genes
caveats: This step needs a curated pathway gene-set collection for human, resolved at run time against WikiPathways (human, 2026.07.10) and MSigDB Hallmark (human, 2026.1); if either is unavailable at run time, report which set was used and skip the other rather than failing silently
WikiPathways GMT lines are '%'-delimited descriptors — split on '%' to recover a readable pathway name before reporting results
steps.question: Which biological pathways are over-represented among genes showing a treatment-specific (condition:time interaction) trajectory, using WikiPathways and Hallmark human gene sets?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g. fgsea or clusterProfiler ORA) is run on the significant interaction gene list from T1S2 against the human WikiPathways GMT and the MSigDB Hallmark human GMT
Gene symbols in the DESeq2 results are matched to the GMT identifier space (HGNC symbols) before testing; report the match rate
Enrichment results include adjusted p-values (BH) and are reported even if no term survives correction — do not omit a null result

If the interaction gene list from T1S2 is empty or very small (e.g. <10 genes), this step reports that enrichment is underpowered/not run rather than fabricating a ranked-list GSEA on non-significant genes

plan.title: DESeq2 LRT for treatment-specific time-course signal
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq counts (12000 genes x 25 samples, salmon-derived integer counts) with a 2-condition x 4-timepoint (t0..t3) design, 3 replicates per cell (metadata: condition, time, time_hours). The research question — which genes change over time in a treatment-specific way, beyond the shared time trend — is exactly the classic DESeq2 likelihood-ratio-test (LRT) time-course design: fit a full model with a condition:time interaction (~condition + time + condition:time) against a reduced model that drops the interaction term (~condition + time), so the LRT isolates genes whose temporal trajectory differs by condition, independent of genes that simply move with time in both arms. This requires (1) loading and QC-filtering the raw counts and aligning them to metadata, (2) running the DESeq2 full-vs-reduced LRT to get an interaction gene list with FDR control, (3) characterizing and visualizing the temporal shape of the significant interaction genes per condition (since the LRT p-value alone doesn't say which time point diverges or in which direction), and (4) functional interpretation of the interaction gene set via pathway enrichment against WikiPathways/Hallmark human gene sets and, if warranted, network context via STRING. All reference sets used are human, matching organism metadata. No PK, safety, immune, or drug-repurposing signal is implied by the research question, so no translational steps are added.
